$285B in SaaS market cap were wiped in 48 hours early this month, everyone says AI is killing SaaS, but that's actually a good thing for SaaS founders!

Last week, I talked about the rewriting of common moats in SaaS, this week, let's talk about the business model we've know since the 2010s, what's cracking and what replaces it: 👇

1. Pure price per seat doesn't work anymore and that's what the market mostly reflects.

If you priced per seat, you are only a tool that will soon only be used by agents and if 1 agent can now do the work of 100 humans, you lost all your revenue. This is what the market foresees for SalesForce, Hubspot or Servicenow.

2. If you are not a tool anymore but selling work, you should theoretically price on outcome

This one's already an old one and you'll learn everything you need about that listnening to Des Traynor. But this only works when the outcome is binary, measurable, and clearly attributable to one system. Support tickets? Yes. Marketing? Sales pipleine? Multi-step workflows? No.

3. If you can't measure outcomes, you are left with hybrid pricing

Base subscription to cover your margin floor + usage on top. ElevenLabs does it. Claude does it. Most AI SDR tools do it. It mixes subscription stability while protecting you from token burn.

4. Usage or outcome based prices, SaaS margins won't be what they used to be.

The entire SaaS flywheel assumed headcount grows → seats grow → revenue grows -> near to zero marginal costs => 80% gross margin. AI flips this. Every LLM query carries variable COGS. Unless token become as commoditized as SaaS infra, the new standard is going to be on tighter margins.

5. But the good news is that you are now selling against labor budgets, not IT budgets.

IT/SaaS spend is 8-12% of enterprise spend. The other 88-92% is people. That's where the money is. When your SaaS is now doing work instead of being just a tool, you're not a software line item anymore. You're a headcount line item. Different buyer, different budget, 10x bigger pool. This is the business model shift that matters more than any pricing mechanic.


TAKEAWAY

Old SaaS: sell a tool -> price per seat -> near-zero marginal costs -> 80% margins, sell against IT budget.

New SaaS: sell work -> price per outcome/usage -> real variable COGS -> tighter margins -> selling against headcount.

Worse margins, but 10x bigger market!
